description: Wire vectors of the three message formats, the byte region that the Produce and the Fetch apis carry: the formats v0 and v1 captured from a Kafka 0.10.2.2 broker, the record batch v2 and the two down-conversions of it from the Kafka 0.11.0.3 broker of this line. Replayed by tests/Compliance.

vectors.description: Three uncompressed records of message format v1 on a topic with the default message.timestamp.type=CreateTime, read back with a Fetch v2 request. Every message carries its own timestamp and the absolute offset the broker assigned to it.

The same three records on a topic configured with message.timestamp.type=LogAppendTime: the broker replaced every timestamp with the time of the append and set bit 3 of the attributes of every message.

A gzip-compressed batch of the same three records, stored as the second batch of the partition: the wrapper message carries the absolute offset 5 of the last inner message and the largest timestamp of the batch, while the inner offsets stay relative (0, 1, 2).
The same batch with the snappy codec, in the xerial block framing that Kafka uses.
The same batch with the lz4 codec: an LZ4 frame with the correct frame descriptor checksum (04 22 4d 18 60 40 82), which is the one message format v1 uses.

A gzip batch on a LogAppendTime topic: the broker rewrote the wrapper message only - its attributes announce the codec and the LogAppendTime type and its timestamp is the append time - while the compressed inner messages keep the CreateTime values of the producer, which the reader has to ignore.

The lz4 batch above, read with a Fetch v1 request: the broker converted the stored message format v1 down to v0, which drops the timestamps, turns the inner offsets into absolute ones (3, 4, 5) and writes the LZ4 frame with the broken descriptor checksum of KAFKA-3160 (04 22 4d 18 60 40 1a).

Three uncompressed records of the message format v2 that the Java console producer wrote into the topic t2-rb-none with the default message.timestamp.type=CreateTime, read out of the log segment of the broker. The three records of the batch differ by their offset and timestamp deltas alone: the batch header carries the base offset, the first timestamp and the largest one, and every record repeats only the difference.

The same three records with --compression-codec gzip. Only the records part is compressed: the 61 header bytes up to and including the record count stay plain, so the batch says how many records it holds without being decompressed.
The same three records with --compression-codec snappy. The records part is a snappy stream in the blocking format of the xerial library, the same framing the message formats v0 and v1 use.

The same three records with --compression-codec lz4. The frame descriptor checksum is the correct 0x82: the KAFKA-3160 breakage applies to the message format v0 alone, and a batch of the format v2 is never written with the broken one.

The same three records on a topic with message.timestamp.type=LogAppendTime. Bit 3 of the attributes is set and maxTimestamp is the time of the append, which is the timestamp of every record of the batch; the broker leaves firstTimestamp and the timestamp deltas of the producer untouched.

Three batches of one record each, of three different codecs, in a single byte region: the log of the topic t2-rb-multi after three separate runs of the console producer. Each batch carries its own base offset, so a reader walks the region batch by batch.

Two records with headers (KIP-82), produced with a raw Produce v3 frame and read back with a raw Fetch v4 frame. The headers show the three shapes a header value has: a byte array, an empty one and a null one; a header key is never null.
Three records that use every combination of an empty and an absent key and value: the varint length -1 is null and the length 0 is the empty byte array, and the broker stores both as they were sent.

The data batch of a committed transaction: bit 4 of the attributes is set, the producer id and the epoch are the ones InitProducerId handed out and baseSequence is 0. Written with the raw sequence InitProducerId, AddPartitionsToTxn, Produce v3 with a transactional id, EndTxn.

The control batch that the transaction coordinator appended when the transaction above was committed: the attributes are 0x30 (transactional and control), the batch holds one record whose key is the version 0 and the type 1 (COMMIT) and whose value is the version 0 and the coordinator epoch 0, and baseSequence is -1. A client never hands such a record to an application.

The log of t2-rb-none - the record batch v2 of messageformat.v2.none.createtime - answered to a Fetch v3 request, which a client that does not understand the message format v2 sends. The broker converts the batch into three uncompressed messages of the message format v1, keeping the offsets and the timestamps.
The same log answered to a Fetch v1 request: three messages of the message format v0, which has no timestamp field at all, so the CreateTime of every record is lost on the way.
